content.text: {"label":"outage","explanation":"The payments surge was caused by the P1 card authorisation gateway incident (INC-20261001-6607, opened 13:00): debit cards were declining with response code 91. In the 15:00-15:45 window, card_declined calls ran at 5.35x normal (264 vs 49 expected) and payment_status_enquiry at 1.58x. General volume and attendance are normal, and no marketing campaign is listed. The incident is now marked resolved and the tail is fading. Payments volume fell from +125% at 14:45 to +24% at 15:45. Staffing is above plan (50 vs 43 agents), and service level has been 100% for the last three intervals.","plan_name":"Outage tail: light-touch safety net","rationale":"Earlier actions plus the fix have restored service: payments has been at 100% for 45 minutes with surplus agents and falling volume. Further spend is not justified. Overtime, more coaching cancellations and more cross-skill moves would add cost with no service gain. A second break delay would only push the deficit into the evening. The outage message should not be renewed because the incident is resolved, and telling customers about a fault that is fixed would mislead them. As a free safeguard against residual card_declined callbacks and customers retrying, IVR callback on payments for 16:00-17:30 only triggers if waits exceed 120 s. Keep monitoring and escalate if volume rebounds.","actions":[{"kind":"ivr_callback","queue":"payments","from_queue":null,"to_queue":null,"start":"16:00","end":"17:30","delay_minutes":null,"agents":null,"agents_offered":null,"mode":"callback","related_reasons":[],"share":null,"reasons":[],"message_text":null}]}
